He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] and was selected 22nd overall by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. In January 2021, he was traded to the Cleveland Cavaliers as part of a four-team blockbuster [[James Harden]] trade. In February 2022, Allen was named to his first [[NBA All-Star Game]]. Allen has the highest [[offensive rating]] (130.1) of any player in NBA history (minimum 15,000 [[Minute (basketball)|minute]]s played).{{Cite web |title=Highest offensive rating in NBA history, minimum 15,000 minutes played |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=highest+offensive+rating+in+nba+history%2C+minimum+15%2C000+minutes+played |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251217043042/https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=highest+offensive+rating+in+nba+history,+minimum+15,000+minutes+played |archive-date=December 17, 2025 |access-date=December 17, 2025 |website=[[StatMuse]]}} ==Early life== Born in [[San Diego]], California,{{cite web|title= Growing Up ... Jarrett Allen|url= https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/features/growingup-allen-211216|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 25, 2025|date=December 16, 2021|last=Gabriele|first=J.}} Allen attended Walsh Middle Player Profiles |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/188079 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 27, 2020}} ==College career== As a freshman at the University of Texas, Allen averaged 13.4 points and 8.4 rebounds per game. However, Texas finished with a disappointing [[2016–17 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|11–22]] record. His best game was a 22-point, 19-rebound performance in a 12-point loss to [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. After the season, he entered the [[2017 NBA draft]] but did not initially hire an agent before deciding to forgo his remaining three years of college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Brian |title=Report: Texas F Jarrett Allen will enter NBA draft but not hire an agent |url=https://www.hookem.com/2017/03/21/report-texas-f-jarrett-allen-will-enter-nba-draft-not-hire-agent/ |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18969359 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 9, 2020 |date=March 21, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn Nets (2017–2021)=== Allen was selected with the 22nd overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets]],{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Select Jarrett Allen 22nd Overall In 2017 NBA Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/06/23/brooklyn-nets-select-jarrett-allen-22nd-overall-2017-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 23, 2017|date=June 23, 2017}} and signed his rookie scale deal with the Nets on July 20.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Jarrett Allen|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/07/20/brooklyn-nets-sign-jarrett-allen|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 27, 2018|date=July 20, 2017}} He was 19 years and 182 days old when he made his NBA debut on October 20, becoming the second-youngest player ever to set foot on the court for the Nets, just behind [[Derrick Favors]].{{cite news|last=Logan|first=Greg|title=Young Jarrett Allen impresses teammates in NBA debut|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/nets/young-jarrett-allen-impresses-teammates-in-nba-debut-t83848|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227213802/https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/nets/young-jarrett-allen-impresses-teammates-in-nba-debut-1.14570050|url-status=live|archive-date=February 27, 2018|access-date=February 27, 2018|publisher=Newsday|date=October 21, 2017}}{{cite news|last=Lewis|first=Brian|title=Nets rookie shows his mettle during crunch time|url=https://nypost.com/2017/10/21/nets-rookie-shows-his-mettle-during-crunch-time/|access-date=February 27, 2018|publisher=New York Post|date=October 21, 2017}} He finished the game with nine points on 3-for-3 shooting, two rebounds and one block. On January 25, 2018, Allen joined the starting lineup for the first time and recorded a career-high 16 points and 12 rebounds in a 116–108 win over the [[2017–18 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|last=Dowd|first=Tom|title=Jarrett Allen Takes Big Strides Into Brooklyn Nets Starting Cavaliers (2021–present)=== On January 14, 2021, Allen was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a multi-player, four-team deal with the Rockets that sent [[James Harden]] to the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire James Harden|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/01/14/brooklyn-nets-acquire-james-harden|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 14, 2021|date=January 14, 2021}} [[File:Jarrett Allen 2022 NBA All-Star.jpg|thumb|Allen at the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]] in Cleveland]] On July 23, 2021, Cleveland extended a qualifying offer to Allen, making him a restricted free agent.{{cite web |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2021/07/cleveland-cavaliers-extend-qualifying-offer-to-jarrett-allen-making-him-restricted-free-agent.html |title=Cleveland Cavaliers extend qualifying offer to Jarrett Allen, making him restricted free agent |last=Fedor |first=Chris |date=July 23, 2021 |website=Cleveland.com |publisher=[[The Plain Dealer]] |access-date=July 23, 2021}} Allen signed a five-year, $100 million contract with Cleveland on August 6.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/allen-extension-210806|title=Cavaliers Sign Jarrett Allen to Multi-Year Extension|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021}} On October 20, 2021, in a 132–121 loss to the [[2021–22 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]], Allen became the first player since the [[shot clock]] was introduced in the [[1954–55 NBA season]] to make 10 or more field goals without a miss in a season-opener.{{cite web|last=Russo |first=Kelsey |title=Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen make history, plus other observations from Cavs' loss to Grizzlies|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2904262/2021/10/21/evan-mobley-and-jarrett-allen-make-history-plus-other-observations-from-cavs-loss-to-grizzlies/|url-status=live|access-date=October 24, 2021|work=The Athletic|date=October 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021132743/https://theathletic.com/2904262/2021/10/21/evan-mobley-and-jarrett-allen-make-history-plus-other-observations-from-cavs-loss-to-grizzlies/ |archive-date=October 21, 2021 }} Allen was named a replacement for Harden, for whom he was traded a year prior, on Team LeBron in the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web|date=February 14, 2022|title=Cleveland's Allen to replace Philadelphia's Harden on Team LeBron in 2022 NBA All-Star Game|url=https://pr.nba.com/clevelands-allen-to-replace-philadelphias-harden-on-team-lebron-in-2022-nba-all-star-game/|access-date=February 14, 2022|website=NBA.com}} Starting all the 56 games he played, Allen finished the 2021–22 season averaging a number of career best with 16.1 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.3 blocks and .8 steals per game, while shooting .677, .100 and .708 from the field, the three-point line and on free throws, respectively, on 32.3 minutes per game. Alongside rookie and fellow Cavalier [[Evan Mobley]], Allen led Cleveland from a .306 winning percentage and the league's sixth-worst defense to a .537 winning percentage and the league's fifth-best defense for efficiency; it was .578 before Allen suffered a fractured finger injury in early March.{{cite web|last=Buckley|first=Zach|date=April 14, 2022|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2955308-grading-every-2022-nba-teams-rookie-class|title=Grading Every 2022 NBA Team's Rookie Class|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=April 15, 2022}} [[File:Jarrett Allen PG.jpg|thumb|Allen in 2023]] On December 28, 2023, he scored 24 points, grabbed 23 rebounds, recorded 6 assists and 2 steals in a 113–110 victory over the [[2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |date=2023-12-28 |title=Cavaliers' Jarrett Allen: Dominates on glass Wednesday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/cavaliers-jarrett-allen-dominates-on-glass-wednesday/ |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} The next day, Allen posted 30 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and two blocks on 15-of-17 shooting from the field in a 119–111 loss against the [[2023–24 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2023 |title=Giannis Antetokounmpo scores 34, leads Bucks to a 119-111 win over the Cavaliers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585061 |access-date=December 31, 2023 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en-US}} On January 22, 2024, he set the franchise record for consecutive double-doubles during a win against the [[2023–24 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]] by passing the 11-game streak held by both [[Andre Drummond]] and [[Elmore Smith]].{{Cite web |date=2024-01-23 |title=Cavs C Jarrett Allen sets franchise record with another double-double night |url=https://www.news5cleveland.com/news/local-news/cavs-c-jarrett-allen-sets-franchise-record-with-another-double-double-night |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=News 5 Cleveland WEWS |language=en}} In game 2 of the Cavaliers' [[2024 NBA playoffs#(4) Cleveland Cavaliers vs. (5) Orlando Magic|first-round playoffs series]] against the Orlando Magic, Allen recorded a playoff career-high 20 rebounds, along with 16 points, three assists, two steals and three blocks in a 96–86 win.{{cite web |date=April 22, 2024 |title=Donovan Mitchell scores 23 as Cavaliers power to 96-86 win over Magic and 2-0 lead in series |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401655118 |access-date=April 30, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On July 31, 2024, Allen and the Cavaliers agreed to a three-year, $91 million max contract extension.{{cite web | last=Young | first=Ryan | title=Cavaliers, center Jarrett Allen reportedly reach 3-year, $91 million max extension | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2024-07-31 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/cavaliers-center-jarrett-allen-reportedly-reach-3-year-91-million-max-extension-200347596.html | access-date=2024-10-05}} He started all 82 games for Cleveland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], posting averages of 13.5 points, 9.7 rebounds and 1.9 assists.{{Cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |date=April 14, 2025 |title=11 NBA iron men who played all 82 games this season, including an old and tiny Chris Paul |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2025/4/14/24408190/nba-players-all-82-games-appear-ironman-chris-paul-mikal-bridges |access-date=July 19, 2025 |website=sbnation.com |language=en}} In October 2025, Allen suffered a left [[ring finger]] injury during the game against the [[2024–25 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]]. After getting assessed, it was confirmed it was a non-displaced fracture of his [[distal phalanx]]{{cite web |title=Jarrett Allen Status Update |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-jarrett-allen-251030 |website=cavs.com |access-date=13 November 2025 |language=en}} On February 2, 2026, Allen recorded a career-high 40 points, 17 rebounds, five assists, two steals and four blocks in a 130–111 win over the [[2024–25 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web |date=February 1, 2026 |title=Jarrett Allen scores career-high 40 points as the Cavaliers beat the Trail Blazers 130-111 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810565 |access-date=February 2, 2026 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On May 3, 2026, Allen tied his playoff career high of 22 points, and added 19 rebounds, as the Cavaliers defeated the [[2025–26 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]] 114–102 in game 7 of the first-round series.{{cite web |author= |date=May 3, 2026 |title=Allen ties playoff career high with 22 points as Cavaliers beat Raptors 114-102 to advance
